label: March 18, 2025
videoTitle: City Council Meeting | March 18th, 2025 | City of Beaumont, CA
timestampBasis: No item video offsets verified. Clock times in official minutes are not video offsets.
sourceCoverage: All 68 City-listed supporting documents matched item by item to the supplied 789-page packet bookmarks. Every report and attachment is linked with its original City URL and packet page range. This verifies the source inventory, not the substantive accuracy of every page. The existing 36 minutes-backed entries, recorded decisions and video link are preserved; published recommendations appear separately.

items.title: City Manager performance evaluation
items.outcome: Deferred until after regular session; the later report-out states no reportable action (minutes pages 9–10).

items.title: City Manager labor negotiations
items.outcome: Deferred until after regular session; the later report-out states no reportable action (minutes pages 9–10).

items.title: Real property negotiations — APN 424-010-007
items.outcome: No reportable action reported. The matter describes approximately 6.26 acres near West 4th Street and SR 60 and negotiations with Lassen Development Partners.

items.title: Regular-session opening and attendance
items.outcome: Called to order at 6:41 p.m. All five Council members listed present. This is a clock time in the minutes, not a video offset.

items.title: Introduction of Interim Police Chief George Walter
items.outcome: Introduction listed in the minutes; no separate motion recorded.

items.title: CSMFO Volunteer of the Year — Jennifer Ustation
items.outcome: Award recognition listed in the minutes; no separate motion recorded.

items.title: Public comment on matters not on the agenda
items.outcome: The minutes record no comments.

items.title: Warrants dated February 28 and March 14, 2025
items.outcome: Ratified with the consent calendar by unanimous vote; motion Fenn, second Martinez.

items.title: March 4, 2025 minutes
items.outcome: Approved with the consent calendar by unanimous vote.

items.title: February City Attorney invoices — $68,343.87
items.outcome: Approved with the consent calendar by unanimous vote. Approval is not proof of payment.

items.title: Corrected FY2024 Gann-limit language
items.outcome: Resolution correcting growth-factor language to non-residential adopted with the consent calendar by unanimous vote.

items.title: Tri Pointe bond exonerations and reductions
items.outcome: Consent approval covers listed public improvements, six maintenance-bond exonerations, 41 performance-bond reductions, and improvement agreements/security for the SCE easement trail, Planning Area 14 basin and Cherry Avenue street lights.

items.title: Easement recordation — APN 424-010-007
items.outcome: Public and private easement recordation across the 6.26-acre City-owned parcel approved with the consent calendar by unanimous vote.

items.title: Youth Council report
items.outcome: Report-out by Youth Council Members Campos and Ivanov.

items.title: Lift-station and force-main sewer code standards
items.outcome: Hearing opened and closed at 6:50 p.m. with no comments. First reading approved unanimously; motion Voigt, second Fenn. Introduction is not final ordinance adoption.

items.title: Economic Development Director employment agreement
items.outcome: Kirk Pelser employment agreement approved unanimously and City Manager authorized to sign; motion Voigt, second Lara.

items.title: Proposed CFD bond refunding criteria
items.outcome: Consensus directed staff and the financing team on savings criteria and to return for ultimate approval. The minutes' phrase “3% savings 200 savings in year 2” is unclear; the per-parcel criterion requires verification against the recording. No specific refunding issuance is established by this direction.

items.title: CFD 2016-3 Series 2025 bonds and acquisition amendment
items.outcome: Resolutions approving an acquisition-agreement amendment and authorizing bonds up to $7.5 million adopted unanimously; motion Voigt, second Fenn. Authorization is not proof of actual issuance.

items.title: Sales-tax allocation and fiscal sustainability planning
items.outcome: Consensus to draft a letter to Cal Cities, copy other cities with Amazon/e-commerce, and move forward with Phase 1 as presented. The minutes do not provide a standalone spending amount here.

items.title: 2025 Cherry Festival sponsorship request
items.outcome: The request was $350,000. Council unanimously approved the budgeted $100,000 by paying the entertainment-invoice balance, directed an agency meeting on further contributions, and requested return April 1; motion White, second Fenn. Do not label the full $350,000 request approved.

items.title: City hosting of the 2025 Cherry Festival Parade
items.outcome: City hosting approved unanimously; motion Fenn, second Martinez.

items.title: Projects for 2025 Congressional appropriations requests
items.outcome: Proposed project list and submission of funding requests approved unanimously; motion White, second Fenn. Submission does not establish a grant award.

items.title: CalSIP stream-gage grant — $108,000
items.outcome: Resolution authorizing the funding request, acceptance and execution adopted unanimously; motion Fenn, second Voigt. Grant amount and acceptance do not establish receipt or expenditure.

items.title: Five-year RAMS financial-audit contract — $337,125
items.outcome: Five-year Rogers, Anderson, Malody and Scott agreement and annual engagement letters approved unanimously; motion White, second Martinez.

items.title: Enterprise Fleet Management agreements
items.outcome: Fleet procurement, leasing, outfitting and vehicle-disposal agreements approved 4–0; Fenn recused/abstained. Motion White, second Voigt. The vote continues on minutes page 8.

items.title: Wastewater plant improvements WW24-01 — reject bids and rebid
items.outcome: Staff authorized unanimously to reject all bids, revise bidding documents and re-advertise; motion Voigt, second White. This was not a construction award.

items.title: Fairway Canyon sewer-failure emergency follow-up
items.outcome: Consensus directed a return at the next meeting with response efforts, expenditures and timeline updates. No completion or final cost is established here.

items.title: Legislative updates
items.outcome: No update recorded.

items.title: Economic Development update
items.outcome: No update recorded.

items.outcome: Report heading listed; minutes do not summarize a separate action.

items.outcome: No report recorded.

items.outcome: Upcoming events shared.

items.title: Future agenda items
items.outcome: Community-center needs, County annexation agreement, sanctuary-city clarification, credit agreements, CRC parking, Financial and Audit Committee ordinance, and development-agreement review listed for later consideration.

items.outcome: Regional-agency and community-meeting report-outs recorded for Fenn, Martinez, White, Voigt and Lara.

items.title: Adjournment and next meeting
items.outcome: Minutes state adjournment at 11:30 p.m. and April 1, 2025 as the next regular meeting. Clock times are not converted to video timestamps; the recording's full coverage has not been independently verified.
